# PEN-3705 — stop forcing `optional: true` on propagated Secret mounts

PR: [#2184](https://github.com/Blockcast/paperclip/pull/2184)

## Files

- `src/server/k8s-client.ts`
- `src/server/k8s-client.test.ts`
- `src/server/job-manifest.ts`
- `src/server/job-manifest.test.ts`

## What changed

`job-manifest.ts` overrode every propagated Secret volume with an unconditional
`optional: true`, discarding the source volume's own setting. It now carries that
setting through, and `k8s-client.ts` captures it off the server pod alongside the
`defaultMode` and `items` it already captured. `undefined` is left unset rather
than coerced to `false` — upstream already reads an absent `optional` as
required, so the source's silence is preserved verbatim rather than restated.

Three tests were added covering the three source states: required-by-silence,
explicit `optional: false`, explicit `optional: true`. Each was checked against
the pre-change source first and fails there, so they discriminate rather than
passing either way.

## Why

The chart declares `github-mcp-token` with no `optional:` field, which upstream
reads as required. Forcing `optional: true` downstream silently dropped that
requirement on every agent Job pod.

For a credential mount that is not graceful degradation, because the env var
naming the token points *inside* the mount and so keeps resolving once the mount
is gone. `PAPERCLIP_GITHUB_TOKEN_FILE` names
`/paperclip/.secrets/github-token/token`; without the mount that path is the bare
shared-PVC directory underneath — mode `2775`, writable by `uid 1000`, the uid
every agent container runs as, on a CephFS volume shared by the whole fleet.
Failing open therefore did not leave the agent with "no credential"; it moved the
credential path to somewhere any agent can write, with nothing signalling that it
had happened.

PEN-3705 is the witness: an agent seat reported no usable GitHub credential while
that path was an empty, group-writable directory, at a time when the Secret
existed and the StatefulSet mounted it non-optionally.

## Behavioural consequence

An agent Job whose GitHub token Secret is missing now fails to start rather than
starting blind. That is intended. It is also inert against the deployed
configuration: both volumes currently on `AGENT_SECRET_VOLUME_ALLOWLIST`
(`paperclip-github-mcp-token`, `authbot-mcp-consumer-service-keys`) are
chart-declared required and both Secrets exist.

A volume that genuinely should tolerate absence still can — it just has to say so
in the chart, where the decision is visible and reviewable, instead of having it
imposed here where it was not.

## Not addressed here

The larger PEN-3705 finding is untouched: the GitHub wrappers seeded into
`/paperclip/.local/bin` (`gh`, `git`, `github-mcp-server`,
`github-token-credential-helper`, `paperclip-github-token-env`) are themselves
mode 755 `node:node` on the shared PVC, and both `/paperclip/.local/bin` and
`/paperclip/bin` precede `/usr/bin` on PATH — a precedence `paperclip.runtimePath`
deliberately enforces so PEN-2527's egress scrubber is not bypassed. A
permissions fix is structurally impossible there, since the `seed` initContainer
that writes them runs `runAsUser: 1000`, making the writer the same uid as the
consumer. Those wrappers need to move into the image, root-owned. Tracked
separately so it does not ride along with this one-field change.

Nor does this reach `/paperclip/.secrets/github-merge-token`, which is a live
instance of the same failure class and should not be read as having been
assessed and found safe. Measured on an agent pod on 2026-10-02: that path is
**not** a mount. It is a bare directory on the shared CephFS PVC, mode 2775
`root:node`, empty, and writable by uid 1000 — while its sibling
`/paperclip/.secrets/github-token` is a correct read-only tmpfs projection whose
directory refuses writes with `EROFS`. It is reachable because
`paperclip-github-merge-token` is deliberately absent from
`AGENT_SECRET_VOLUME_ALLOWLIST` (removed in #1411, correctly: propagating a
review-clearing credential made "can clear branch protection" a fleet-wide
capability on 108 agent Job pods). Never being propagated is exactly why this
change cannot help it — the volume never reaches `buildJobManifest`, so getting
`optional:` right there has nothing to act on. What this change fixes is a
mount that goes missing; what remains is a path that was never mounted. Tracked
as PEN-3731.

A note on reading that directory pair, since a `stat`-only look inverts the
conclusion: the mounted sibling reports mode 1777, which is the tmpfs root
default rather than a deliberately set sticky bit. The protection there is the
`ro` mount, which `findmnt` shows and `stat` does not. A sticky bit alone would
only prevent unlinking another user's entry, not creating a new name in an empty
directory — so it would not be a control against this failure class at all.
